name: Echo CS-400
blurb: 40.2 cc homeowner saw on 3/8″ low-profile .050″ chain. 18″ bar: 62 drive links (Echo's catalog). 16″ bar: Oregon says 56 drive links, Echo's own chart says 57 — so we flag it.
intro: The CS-400 is Echo's 40.2 cc homeowner saw, and like most saws in its class it runs 3/8″ low-profile chain — the smaller “Picco-class” profile, not the full-size 3/8″ of its bigger brother the CS-590. Echo's own catalog chart lists a 16″ and an 18″ bar for it, both on .050″ gauge with a 5/32″ file. The 18″ setup is 62 drive links. The 16″ setup is the one to check: Oregon's chain data fits the CS-400 with a 56-link loop, but Echo's chart lists 57 for the 16″ bar, so count before you buy.

sources.title: Product data for 91VXL056G / 91PX056G (3/8″ Low Profile, .050″ gauge, 56 drive links, 5/32″ file; fitments include Echo CS-400; cross-references to Husqvarna H37-56 and Stihl 63 PM3 56)
ECHO chainsaws catalog (Jan 2023) — “Bars and Chains” chart: CS-400 16″ bar 16A0CD3757C with chain 91PX57CQ (57 drive links); 18″ bar 18A0CD3762C with chain 91PX62CQ (62 drive links)

sources_note: Oregon product data for 91VXL056G / 91PX056G (fitments include Echo CS-400) and Echo's 2023 catalog bars-and-chains chart, which disagree by one drive link on the 16″ bar — checked Oct 2026.

bars.note: Pitch and gauge agree, but the drive-link count does not: Oregon's chain data fits the CS-400 with its 56-link loop (91PX056), while Echo's own 2023 catalog lists the CS-400's 16″ bar (16A0CD3757C) with the 57-link chain 91PX57CQ. Count the drive links on your bar stamp or old chain before ordering.
Echo's 2023 catalog lists an 18″ bar (18A0CD3762C) with chain 91PX62CQ: 3/8″ low-profile, .050″ gauge, 62 drive links, 5/32″ file. Oregon's S62 is the same 62-link spec.
